assertions.name: handbuild_chi_matches_repo_symbolic_route
assertions.source: Route A: trace of σ₁σ₂σ₁ from the hand-built Hoefsmit matrices in this module. Route B: chi_lambda_braid(..., precision='symbolic_q') from hecke_characters_symbolic. Exact rational functions of q, compared symbolically — the reconciliation the recorded Blocker B called out of scope.

assertions.name: pr1851_reference_column_is_single_crossing_character
assertions.source: Route A: the three reference numbers recorded in this module's docstring as PR #1851 pyhecke output at q₀. Route B: χ_λ(σ₁) at q₀ from the repo symbolic route (= q, q−1/q, −1/q). Match band 1e-6 relative — three orders tighter than the alleged 24% and eight orders looser than exact, so it distinguishes 'same quantity' from 'same to transcription precision'.

assertions.name: python_fallback_chi_at_muon_anchor_matches_kernel
assertions.source: Route A: chi_lambda_braid at q_μ with _RUST_CHI_AVAILABLE forced False — the Python seminormal fallback the recorded Blocker A says raises ValueError for q ≠ q₀. Route B: the same character from the mpfr kernel. Tolerance 1e-12 is the f64 grade of Route A, not a precision claim. This assertion is unformable if Blocker A holds.

assertions.name: braid_relation_holds_for_handbuilt_sigmas
assertions.source: Route A: σ₁σ₂σ₁ from the hand-built Hoefsmit matrices. Route B: σ₂σ₁σ₂ from the same matrices. Symbolic in q, over all three Wedderburn blocks of H_3.

assertions.name: hecke_quadratic_relation_holds_for_handbuilt_sigmas
assertions.source: Route A: σ² by matrix multiplication. Route B: h·σ + I with h = q − 1/q, the Hecke quadratic relation (σ − q)(σ + 1/q) = 0. Both generators of all three blocks, symbolic in q.

assertions.name: cross_anchor_chi_delta_matches_derivative_quadrature
assertions.source: Route A: Σ_λ |χ^λ(q_μ) − χ^λ(q_p)| by direct subtraction of two ['mpfr_50dps'] evaluations. Route B: Σ_λ |∫ dχ^λ/dq dq| across the anchor interval by mpmath quadrature of the exact symbolic derivative — no subtraction of nearly equal numbers anywhere.

description: Stage B: cross-anchor (proton vs muon) stability of the per-Wedderburn-block χ^λ(electron word). The three infrastructure blockers this probe used to record as fact are re-tested at run time — the Python fallback's q ≠ q₀ guard is gone, pyhecke_native is importable, and the '24% convention mismatch' was the recorded reference column being χ_λ(σ₁) rather than χ_λ(σ₁σ₂σ₁). The test therefore runs, by two independent routes at each anchor.

B_handbuild_convention_mismatch.measured: no mismatch — the recorded reference column is chi_lambda(sigma_1), not chi_lambda(sigma_1 sigma_2 sigma_1); against the same word the hand-build and the repo route agree exactly

verdict.stage_b_status: RAN — every recorded blocker re-tested; A and C stale, B a braid-word misattribution rather than a convention conflict
verdict.open_question: interpretation: (2,1) carries no signal (χ ≡ 0), (3,) and (1,1,1) move at first order in Δq/q. Whether that clears the PR #1836 scalar gate is a threshold question.

caveats: The comment above Q_PROTON_STR says 'Q_MUON - Q_PROTON is ~1.28e-11 from two values that agree to 11 digits'. Measured: Δq = 1.279861919e-8 ≈ 1.28e-8, and the two anchors agree to 8 significant digits, not 11. The mantissa is right and the exponent is three orders out. The comment's conclusion still holds in direction — float64 subtraction of these two anchors loses about half its digits — but the severity it states is overstated, and the '5 significant digits' figure that follows from 1.28e-11 is not what this anchor pair actually costs.
